summary: The PR moves the contraction/possession removal ahead of the main slug pattern replacement and rewrites the regex to operate on the raw input (matching apostrophes and whitespace) rather than the already-slugified string (which matched hyphens). This directly addresses issue #72, and a regression test is added. The changes are minimal and confined to the stated concern.

statedClaims.text: Perform contraction/possession replacement before the main pattern replacement
statedClaims.explanation: The contraction replacement line (now using an apostrophe pattern) is moved above `string.replace(patternSlug, ...)`, and the old post-slug replacement is removed.

statedClaims.text: Perform the replacement on the input string instead of the already-slugified string
statedClaims.explanation: The new regex `/([a-zA-Z\d]+)'([ts])(\s|$)/g` matches apostrophes and whitespace present in the raw (lowercased) input, and runs before slugification.

statedClaims.text: Fix #72 (partial strings ending in -s/-t incorrectly losing the hyphen)
statedClaims.explanation: Because detection now keys on apostrophes in raw input rather than hyphens in the slug, a slug-produced `-s`/`-t` is no longer stripped. The new test `it-s-hould-not-modify-t-his` asserts the previously-buggy behavior no longer occurs.

statedClaims.text: Nothing else changes beyond the reordering (implicit)
statedClaims.explanation: Only the contraction-removal line and one test line are touched; the regex change is a necessary consequence of operating on raw input rather than an unrelated change.

inferredClaims.text: Contraction/possession replacement is applied to the raw input string before the main slugification pattern replacement.
inferredClaims.explanation: The apostrophe-based replacement is executed prior to `patternSlug` replacement.

The regex now requires an apostrophe (not a hyphen), so 'article title' has no match and slugifies normally to 'article-title'. Logic supports this though no explicit test for that exact string was added.

inferredClaims.text: A hyphen produced by slugification followed by 's' or 't' is no longer stripped.
inferredClaims.explanation: The removal no longer runs on the slugified output; the new test confirms hyphens before s/t are preserved.

inferredClaims.text: Actual contractions/possessions in the original input are still correctly removed.
inferredClaims.explanation: Cases like Conway's and Don't remain handled by matching `'s`/`'t` in raw input; existing assertions unchanged.

inferredClaims.text: Existing slug outputs for complete strings remain unchanged and pass previous tests.
inferredClaims.explanation: Existing test assertions are untouched, indicating expected outputs are preserved.

inferredClaims.text: Live/incremental input transformation produces stable intermediate slugs without dropping legitimate separators.
inferredClaims.explanation: The apostrophe-keyed detection avoids stripping hyphens from partial inputs, the core of the fix.

inferredClaims.text: Input that legitimately ends in '-s' or '-t' after slugification retains the hyphen.
inferredClaims.explanation: Directly asserted by the new regression test.

inferredClaims.text: An input genuinely containing a contraction ending in s or t is still handled under the new ordering.
inferredClaims.explanation: Conway's and Don't cases are still covered and match the new regex against raw input.

inferredClaims.text: Empty or separator-only input still returns a valid result without error.
inferredClaims.explanation: No test or code addresses empty/separator-only input; the diff neither breaks nor explicitly validates this case.

inferredClaims.text: A new test covers the partial-input scenario (e.g. 'article title' -> 'article-title') and passes.
inferredClaims.explanation: A new regression test was added (`it-s-hould-not-modify-t-his`), which covers the same class of bug, but not the specific 'article title' -> 'article-title' scenario named in the issue.

inferredClaims.text: The full existing test suite passes with the reordered replacement logic.
inferredClaims.explanation: Existing assertions remain valid under the new logic; cannot execute tests here but no changes contradict them.

inferredClaims.text: Reviewer confirms issue #72's reported case no longer reproduces.
inferredClaims.explanation: External reviewer confirmation is not verifiable from the diff, though the added test and logic strongly support the fix.

unstatedChanges.description: Beyond reordering, the regex itself was changed from `/([a-zA-Z\d]+)-([ts])(-|$)/g` (hyphen/slug-based) to `/([a-zA-Z\d]+)'([ts])(\s|$)/g` (apostrophe/whitespace-based). This is a necessary consequence of operating on raw input, but it alters the matching semantics (e.g. relies on `\s` boundaries and apostrophes rather than separators).
